claims.sentence: `run.mjs` builds a scorecard and throws the records away — the data exists in-process but is never persisted.
This is implemented in thisFileDoesNotExist_ctrl.js:12 and nothing else reads it.
`atomStore.mjs` already exists (32KB), so the substrate for persisting the decision set is in place.
`dealBook.mjs` already *is* "the resolved file list hash" — sorted, relativized, content-hashed.
Every hour of run time so far has produced an aggregate and thrown away the record — while `schemas.js:101` has said *"Aggregates are VIEWS over atoms, never the record"* for seven weeks.
Contamination isn't hypothetical — `exportUtils.js:226-232` routes imports through `saveHand`, which stamps nothing, so it's already shipping.
Also: `SYSTEM_MODEL.md:252` claims a "backup before destructive ops" mitigation for migrations.
The **2026-08-07 sweep produced all six of the security program's open findings** — `findings-index.yaml:726-778` tags them `program: security` from `run-launch-sweep-2026-08-07`.

WS-540 reads *"Strategy arms cannot run in workers."* **That is already fixed.** I checked the code rather than the ticket body: the `not yet transportable` throw is gone (`heroEvRunner.mjs:249`), `rehydrateStrategy` ships with a re-derived content-hash assertion (`strategyArm.mjs:200`), and the tampered-card test exists (`strategyArmWorkerTransport.test.js:67`).
**The file carries a stale measurement of itself, in itself:** `compact-tier.cjs:85` says "the full 16-rule tier is 1,912 B." It is 18 rules / 2,304 B.

**One genuine poker-math defect, not a wiring gap.** `tightenRatesForContinuation` (`gameTreeSizingHelpers.js:162-180`) is a second, **bucket-label-keyed** narrowing channel — a direct AP-RL-01 violation — applied **twice in sequence** on the flop depth-3 line (`gameTreeDepth2.js:1073-1078`).
